queries.label: Why each part matters
expected_rows: "People need to know where information can travel and what authority accompanies an exchange. Naming, transport and permission should be inspectable instead of being collapsed into a single login."@en-AU

"A shared term is useful only if people can discover what it means and where it came from. Clear definitions help communities, developers and institutions discuss the same subject without silently changing it."@en-AU
"Care and shared work involve changing needs and relationships. Keeping who may do what, for whom and under which conditions visible helps people cooperate without losing their own voice."@en-AU

"Understanding a place means relating living things, physical conditions and human activity. Keeping those relationships inspectable helps an attractive landscape become a place to learn and investigate."@en-AU
"Spatial explanations can help people understand a body and discuss support needs. Their usefulness depends on recognisable structure and clear limits, not just on producing a renderable file."@en-AU
"Creators should be able to revise a work while keeping its sources and meaning available. A project should remain understandable to its collaborators and future maintainers."@en-AU

"A useful computing environment should make the next action understandable and let people work towards their own purposes. It should make room for assistance, review and changing circumstances."@en-AU

"A human centric ecosystem still needs to read and use the existing web. Clear boundaries help people move between documents and applications without making every embedded page equally trusted."@en-AU
"People need to understand why a result appeared, question its sources and correct mistakes. Those same capabilities help a developer trace a fault and help an organisation explain a decision."@en-AU
"A person can revisit how a result was produced, and a developer can reproduce or repair it. That helps creative work remain editable and makes technical explanations more concrete."@en-AU

"People should be able to see what was computed and what an observation can support. Device limits and uncertain measurements matter when a visualisation is used to understand the physical world."@en-AU

"An impressive picture is more useful when its underlying work is inspectable and reproducible. Creators can continue editing; reviewers can distinguish a generated illustration from an acquired measurement."@en-AU
"Software should respond honestly to the computer someone has. Reporting a limit or choosing a qualified path is more useful than displaying a control that silently does something else."@en-AU

"People need interfaces that explain changes, remain usable under real device constraints and offer more than one way to reach a task. That work belongs in the application framework as well as individual pages."@en-AU

"The same underlying work can support an illustration, an accessible explanation and an inspectable technical instrument. It need not become a disconnected promotional image each time it changes form."@en-AU
"People and communities need understandable choices about where a service runs, who maintains it and how shared costs and responsibilities are handled."@en-AU

queries.label: Inspect each module's human-agency considerations
expected_rows: "Support should preserve agency rather than assume unlimited substitute authority. Real consent, revocation and consequential-decision evidence need to be exercised in the eventual native workflow."@en-AU

"Application controls must preserve the difference between a person's choices and another party's authority. An accessible explanation and a visible result are part of meaningful control, not merely visual decoration."@en-AU
"Educational models should support comprehension and dignity. They must not imply a diagnosis, a personal body measurement or clinical validation that the source does not establish."@en-AU

"Context, provenance and permission checks support informed use of information. They are tools for implementing safeguards, not a blanket guarantee that every application meets human rights obligations."@en-AU
"Encoding an instrument is not the same as resolving a legal question or enforcing a right. Preserve its source and scope, and show exactly which authored rule an evaluator applied."@en-AU

"Authorship, attribution and permission to use a source need to survive editing and export. The website must show these relationships in a real workflow before claiming the authoring experience complete."@en-AU

"Origin isolation and delegated permissions are practical places to enforce boundaries. The website must demonstrate actual refusal and authorised access before claiming a particular guardianship or privacy outcome."@en-AU

"Keeping source and provenance with a work helps preserve attribution and permitted use. A successful replay proves reproducibility of the recorded production, not ownership of every possible input."@en-AU

"A composition must retain source terms and the meaning of its data across transformations. Availability of an operation is separate from permission to publish its inputs or from artistic acceptance of its output."@en-AU

"Access to a sensor or accelerator does not confer permission to observe a person. Sensing needs a declared purpose and appropriate authority; technical output must not be mistaken for consent."@en-AU
"A device identifier is not a person. Hardware observations can inform a policy decision, but must not replace a person's agency or become an undeclared tracking mechanism."@en-AU
"Naming a capability does not itself grant authority to use personal information or a device. Host admission and a person's permission remain separate responsibilities."@en-AU

"A hosting account must not be treated as the whole person. Isolation, delegated authority and accountability need end-to-end evidence, especially when a service acts for a family or cooperative."@en-AU

"Sensitive ecological and community knowledge needs appropriate authority and careful disclosure. A public scene should not expose private travel or imply that a species was observed where an artist placed it."@en-AU

"Supporting different needs requires tested navigation, understandable state and accessible alternatives. A framework's architectural intention is not proof that every application already provides them."@en-AU

"A cryptographic handle identifies a particular technical relationship, not the entirety of a person. Human agency and disclosure limits must survive changes of device, network and institution."@en-AU

queries.label: How the module groups work together
Inspect Poet and its ownership boundary
expected_rows: "separate Poet application owner not reconciled; shared QualiaDB host mapped"@en-AU

"Poet is the authoring application associated with projects, documents and creative work in the ecosystem. Its role is to help people shape a work, while shared libraries supply the underlying language, knowledge and production services."@en-AU

"Authorship, attribution and permission to use a source need to survive editing and export. The website must show these relationships in a real workflow before claiming the authoring experience complete."@en-AU
"Creators should be able to revise a work while keeping its sources and meaning available. A project should remain understandable to its collaborators and future maintainers."@en-AU
"A planned exhibit will follow a creator changing one scene while keeping its sources, attribution and earlier version available to collaborators."@en-AU

"Shared host implementation is source-mapped in QualiaDB. The separate Poet application repository and current application release still require owner reconciliation; no complete Poet UI demo is claimed."@en-AU

"Poet is the place for shaping and revising a work; Synth is the producer that turns its recipes into deliverable resources. Keeping editing and production distinct lets a creator revisit the work without losing the account of how an earlier version was made."@en-AU

queries.label: Inspect networking scope without a public-mesh claim
expected_rows: "People need to know where information can travel and what authority accompanies an exchange. Naming, transport and permission should be inspectable instead of being collapsed into a single login."@en-AU

"QDNF supplies native protocol libraries for exchanging information between devices: establishing sessions, routing messages and recognising the authority attached to an exchange. Related identifier policy remains within QualiaDB."@en-AU
"Native protocol sources are mapped. No public relay mesh, raw-Ethernet path or full QDNF website experiment is claimed by this module catalogue."@en-AU

"The rules for an exchange are kept separate from the particular connection carrying it. That allows authority and disclosure conditions to be examined alongside a message path, rather than assuming that being connected is enough."@en-AU
"A planned exhibit will follow a limited exchange between devices and show a real refusal when the requested action falls outside the stated authority."@en-AU

"A cryptographic handle identifies a particular technical relationship, not the entirety of a person. Human agency and disclosure limits must survive changes of device, network and institution."@en-AU
"source repositories identified; runtime scope separately qualified"@en-AU
